alignments.note: The ASV wrote one English word for πᾶς ὃς ἄν, and rule 50 records ὃς ἄν → *whosoever* as a single unit in which *who-* answers to the relative and *-soever* to the particle, leaving nothing for the quantifier. Joining all three tokens into one unit remains defensible; rule 2 argues against it.
Relative compressed with the modal particle into a single *-soever* word (rule 50).
The verb's object is the accusative τὸ ὄνομα, which English realizes with no preposition, so *upon* is the verb's own government (rule 106); headed on the lexical verb.
Anarthrous genitive; the supplied determiner and the case preposition both ride with the noun, no article standing (rules 21, 51).
Future passive with auxiliaries, headed on the lexical verb (rule 9).

review_notes: Three source tokens face one English word: rule 50's ὃς ἄν → *whosoever* takes it and πᾶς is left unrepresented, with the competing whole-cluster reading named in the unit's note.
